title: Preparation of Extracellular Matrix Protein Fibers for Brillouin Spectroscopy
protocol: Sacrifice a rat by intra-peritoneal injection of 100 mg/kg of body weight sodium pentobarbitone.
Sever the tail directly at the point of contact with the body, pressing down with a single-edge razor blade.
Wrap the tail in cling film and store it frozen at -20 °C until required.
Collect the tail from the freezer, cut a 20 mm long segment from the proximal end whilst still frozen.
Leave the segment to thaw in a Petri dish filled with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) solution (pH 7.4) at RT.
Thaw the tail.
Make an incision along the length of the tail segment using a scalpel.
Peel back the skin to reveal tendon bundles.
Gently draw each fiber out of its sheath using fine forceps.
Place the drawn fibers in a vial containing distilled water with 0.01% w/v sodium azide (NaN3).
Store the vials refrigerated.
Immerse the fibers in 0.125 U/ml chondroitinase ABC in 0.05 M Tris buffer and 0.06 M sodium acetate at pH 8.0 for 24 hours at 37 °C in a shaking incubator at 200 rpm.
Immerse the fibers in 1 U/ml streptomyces hyaluronidase in 0.05 M Tris buffer and 0.15 M sodium chloride at pH 6.0 for 24 hours at 37 °C in a shaking incubator at 200 rpm.
Immerse the fibers in 1 mg/ml trypsin in 0.05 M sodium phosphate and 0.15 M NaCl at pH 7.2 for 16 hours at 37 °C in a shaking incubator at 200 rpm.
Store purified fibers refrigerated in vials containing distilled water with 0.01% NaN3 until required.
Obtain bovine nuchal ligament from the abattoir, wrap it in cling film and store it frozen at -20°C until use.
Allow the wrapped ligament to thaw at room temperature.
Use a scalpel to defat the thawed ligament.
Add a 0.1 M solution of sodium hydroxide to the defatted ligament in a conical flask, covering the tissue completely.
Boil the flask containing the ligament and NaOH solution in a water bath at 95°C for 45 min.
Remove the ligament from the digestion flask and wash it repeatedly with distilled water until pH 7.0 is achieved.
Submerge the washed ligament in distilled water mixed with 0.01% NaN3 to prevent bacterial growth, and store refrigerated.
Collect the tissue block from the refrigerator carefully using tweezers without applying too much force.
Gently pull smaller elastin segments (20 to 50 mm long, ca. 2 mm thick) away from the larger block and place them in a Petri dish with PBS solution (pH 7.4).
Using fine forceps, gently tease small fiber bundles around 1 mm thick and cut them into lengths of a few mm.
Transfer the fibers to vials containing distilled water mixed with 0.01% NaN3 and store refrigerated until required for measurement.
Cut a piece of reflective silicone slide with a diamond cutter.
Cut a strip of Parafilm to fit over the silicone slide with a hollow cut in the center and place it onto the silicone substrate.
Remove fibers from the refrigerator and collect a single fiber from the storage solution using fine forceps.
Place the collected fiber in a small Petri dish filled with pure water at room temperature for 5 minutes to wash the sample.
Transfer the washed fiber to the center of the parafilm hollow on the silicone substrate.
Place a thin glass coverslip over the fiber.
Pass a heated soldering iron gently over the glass surface to melt the Parafilm beneath and seal the chamber.
Place the sealed chamber on a flat surface under a small weight for approximately 12 hours to ensure good contact between the sample and silicon substrate.
Remove the weight and secure the chamber in place on the substrate using screws.
Mount the sample prepared as in part 1.3 onto a vertical holder equipped with a goniometer.
Enable in-plane rotation of the sample while maintaining a constant scattering angle (2Φ = 90°).
Perform an accurate focus adjustment of the laser light on the sample through the lens.
Set the laser output power to approximately 76 mW on the sample.
Position the sample at a 45° angle (Φ) to the incident laser beam using a Vernier scale.
Run a measurement and maximize the intensity of the peaks in the spectrum.
Open the software for acquisition and manipulation of the data.
Set up the acquisition of a Brillouin spectrum of the sample.
Align the two Fabry-Perot interferometers independently by changing the voltages applied to the piezo by the control unit.
Observe the light reflected by each FP.
Adjust the voltages until the intensity reflected by both FPs tends to zero, indicating correct alignment.
Measure the distance between the two mirrors of the first FP cavity using a dial-gauge.
Calculate the free spectral range (FSR) through FSR = c/2L, where c is the speed of light and L is the measured distance.
Synchronize the scans of the two FP interferometers.
Switch the optical system to the tandem multipass configuration.
Maintain alignment of the two FPs during measurement by automatically controlling the transmitted laser light intensity.
Control the temperature and hydration of the sample carefully to ensure reproducibility of the Brillouin spectrum.
Start the acquisition of a Brillouin spectrum of the sample.
Run the acquisition until a good signal-to-noise ratio is achieved.
Select the spectral range for the peak of interest in the Brillouin spectrum.
Enable a baseline in the fit if the spectral background is much higher than zero.
Ensure that the correction is applied in a systematic and reproducible manner.
Apply a detailed least squares fitting using a DHO function to the Brillouin peak of interest iteratively until convergence is achieved.
Save the fit results to file.
Obtain average values from the fit parameters of the two peaks of each Brillouin doublet.
Calculate the acoustic wave velocity from the peak frequency.
Plot the fit results through graphs, e.g., acoustic wave velocity vs. angle to fiber axis.
Apply relevant models to extract mechanical quantities such as elasticity tensor coefficients.
